questions.text: In a row of students, Rohan is 12th from the left end and 18th from the right end. If 5 students leave the row from the right end, what will be Rohan's new position from the right end?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Total students = (Left Rank + Right Rank) - 1 = 12 + 18 - 1 = 29. After 5 leave from right, New Total = 24. Rohan's Left Rank remains 12. New Right Rank = New Total - Left Rank + 1 = 24 - 12 + 1 = 13. Full: Formula Total = L + R - 1. Removal from right reduces total and right rank by same count (5). New Right = Old Right - 5 = 18 - 5 = 13 (since left rank fixed).

questions.text: In the following question, a statement is given followed by four conclusions. Assuming the statement to be true, decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s). Statement: P ≤ Q < R = S ≥ T > U Conclusions: I. P < R II. S > U III. Q < S IV. R > U

options.label: C
options.text: Only I, II and III follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Write the chain as P ≤ Q < R = S ≥ T > U. Trace each conclusion: I (P<R) follows because P≤Q<R. II (S>U) follows because S≥T>U. III (Q<S) follows because Q<R=S. IV (R>U) follows because R=S≥T>U. All four conclusions hold true. Full Solution: From statement, P ≤ Q and Q < R, so P < R (I true). R = S and S ≥ T > U, so S > U (II true) and R > U (IV true). Q < R and R = S, so Q < S (III true). Hence all conclusions follow.

questions.text: Statements: 1. Some pens are pencils. 2. All pencils are erasers. 3. No eraser is a marker. Conclusions: I. Some pens are not markers. II. All pens are erasers. III. Some pencils are markers. Which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Draw minimal Venn or apply rules. Some pens are pencils + All pencils are erasers ⇒ Some pens are erasers. No eraser is marker ⇒ Those pens are not markers ⇒ I follows. All pens are erasers cannot be concluded (only some pens are pencils) ⇒ II does not follow. All pencils are erasers + No eraser is marker ⇒ No pencil is marker ⇒ III does not follow. Hence only conclusion I follows.

questions.text: In the following sentence, one part may contain a grammatical error. Identify the part with the error. If there is no error, choose 'No error'. The new guidelines require all employees to attend the workshop, but they also insist on to submit a feedback form within a week.

options.label: A
options.text: The new guidelines require all employees to attend the workshop,

options.label: B
options.text: but they also insist on to submit

options.label: C
options.text: a feedback form within a week

questions.solution: Shortcut: After the preposition 'on', a gerund (verb+ing) is required. 'Insist on to submit' uses an infinitive, which is incorrect. The correct form is 'insist on submitting'. Step‑by‑step: The sentence has three segments. Segment A is grammatically sound. Segment B contains 'insist on to submit'; the phrase 'insist on' must be followed by a gerund, so 'to submit' is wrong. Segment C is fine. Hence the error lies in segment B.

questions.text: The difference between Compound Interest (compounded annually) and Simple Interest on a certain sum of money at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹400. What is the principal sum?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For 2 years, Difference (CI - SI) = P × (R/100)². Here, 400 = P × (10/100)² = P × 1/100 ⇒ P = 400 × 100 = ₹40,000. Full Method: SI for 2 years = (P × 10 × 2)/100 = 0.2P. Amount in CI = P(1 + 10/100)² = 1.21P, so CI = 0.21P. Difference = 0.21P - 0.2P = 0.01P = 400 ⇒ P = 40,000.

questions.text: What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following expression? 39.98% of 449.9 + 19.97% of 299.8 - √1680.9 = ?
Statement: A ≥ B > C = D ≤ E < F Conclusions: I. A > D II. C < F III. B ≥ E

options.label: A
options.text: Only Conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution: Shortcut: Trace the chain without breaking direction. A ≥ B > C = D ⇒ A > D (True). C = D ≤ E < F ⇒ C < F (True). B > C = D ≤ E ⇒ relation between B and E is B > D ≤ E (opposing signs), so B ≥ E is False. Full: Decode symbols: A is greater/equal to B; B strictly greater than C; C equals D; D less/equal to E; E strictly less than F. Combine: A > D (via B>C=D). C < F (via D≤E<F). B vs E: B > D and D ≤ E gives no definite relation.

questions.text: In the following questions, two equations numbered I and II are given. Solve both equations and mark the appropriate option. I. 2x² - 11x + 12 = 0 II. 2y² - 13y + 20 = 0
questions.solution: Shortcut: Signs of both equations are (-, +), so roots are positive. Factorize I: (2x-3)(x-4)=0 → x = 1.5, 4. Factorize II: (2y-5)(y-4)=0 → y = 2.5, 4. Since x=4 equals y=4, but x=1.5 < y=2.5, no consistent relation exists. Full: Roots of I: 4, 1.5. Roots of II: 4, 2.5. Comparing: 4 = 4, 4 > 2.5, 1.5 < 4, 1.5 < 2.5. As x can be greater than, less than, or equal to y, the relationship cannot be established.

questions.text: A boat takes 8 hours to cover a certain distance upstream and 6 hours to cover the same distance downstream. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Time ratio Up:Down = 8:6 = 4:3 → Speed ratio Down:Up = 4:3 (inverse). Let Downstream = 4x, Upstream = 3x. Stream speed = (4x-3x)/2 = x/2 = 4 → x=8. Boat speed = (4x+3x)/2 = 3.5x = 28 km/h. Step-by-step: Distance = Speed × Time. Up×8 = Down×6 → Up/Down = 3/4. Down = Up + 2×Stream. Solving gives Up=24, Down=32. Boat = (24+32)/2 = 28.

questions.text: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase underlined in the sentence. The peace talks between the two nations have been **on the back burner** for over a decade.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Context Clue & Idiom Knowledge. 'On the back burner' is a fixed idiom meaning low priority. The duration 'over a decade' supports a state of inactivity/delay, not completion or cancellation. Step-by-step: 1. Recall idiom meaning: 'Back burner' (stove) = low heat/simmering = low priority. 2. Analyze context: 'Talks... for over a decade' implies prolonged pause. 3. Eliminate A (completed), B (supervision), D (cancelled). 4. Option C matches 'low priority/postponed'.

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate phrasal verb to fill in the blank: The manager asked the team to ______ the proposal before submitting it to the board.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate options that do not mean 'review quickly'. 'Look up' means search for information, 'look after' means take care of, 'look into' means investigate. Only 'look over' means examine or review. Step‑by‑step: The context requires a verb meaning 'review' before submission. 'Look over' fits this meaning perfectly. The other phrasal verbs convey different actions and are contextually inappropriate. Therefore, 'look over' is the correct choice.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price. He then allows two successive discounts of 15% and 10% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Net successive discount = 15 + 10 - (15×10)/100 = 23.5%. Marked price = 140% of CP. Selling price = 140 × (1 - 0.235) = 107.1% of CP. Profit% = 7.1%. Full solution: Let CP = ₹100. MP = ₹140. After 15% discount, price = 140 × 0.85 = ₹119. After further 10% discount, SP = 119 × 0.90 = ₹107.1. Profit = ₹7.1 on ₹100, i.e., 7.1%.

questions.text: Select the option that best improves the underlined part of the sentence: The new training program not only enhances technical skills but also developing leadership qualities.
questions.solution: Shortcut: The correlative conjunction 'not only … but also' demands parallel structure. The first part uses the singular verb 'enhances', so the second part must use the same form 'develops'. Step‑by‑step: Identify the verb form after 'not only' – 'enhances' (third‑person singular). To maintain parallelism, the verb after 'but also' must also be third‑person singular 'develops'. Option A provides this parallel form. Option B uses plural 'develop', Option C repeats the gerund 'developing', and Option D changes the conjunction to 'and also', breaking the correlative pair. Hence Option A is correct.

questions.text: If 'A @ B' means 'A is the father of B', 'A # B' means 'A is the sister of B', 'A $ B' means 'A is the mother of B', and 'A % B' means 'A is the brother of B', then how is P related to T in the expression: P @ Q # R $ S % T?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Trace generation gaps backwards from T. S % T ⇒ S is brother of T (Same gen). R $ S ⇒ R is mother of S (Gen +1). Q # R ⇒ Q is sister of R (Same gen). P @ Q ⇒ P is father of Q (Gen +1). Total Gen gap = +2 (Grandfather). Line: P → Q/R (Mother side) ⇒ Maternal Grandfather. Full Solution: Decode step-by-step: 1. S % T means S is the brother of T. 2. R $ S means R is the mother of S, so R is the mother of T. 3. Q # R means Q is the sister of R, so Q is the maternal aunt of T. 4. P @ Q means P is the father of Q, so P is the father of T's maternal aunt. Therefore, P is the Maternal Grandfather of T.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given group of words. A person who travels on foot
questions.solution: Elimination: Options (A), (B), and (C) refer to operators of specific vehicles (car, aircraft, ship/boat) and do not imply travel 'on foot'. Option (D) 'Pedestrian' is derived from Latin 'pedester' (going on foot) and precisely defines a person walking rather than travelling in a vehicle.
